questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
In an economy, no one can be made better off without making someone else worse off. What does not necessarily follow from this?

options.A: The conditions for allocative efficiency have been met.
options.B: The conditions for productive efficiency have been met.
options.C: The distribution of income is socially acceptable.
options.D: The economy is operating at a point on its production possibility curve.

questions.questionText: A government decided to approve a road building scheme because it was socially beneficial. In making its decision it calculated private costs at $800m, private benefits at $800m and external costs at $150m. What must have been true about the external benefits of the scheme?

options.A: External benefits equalled private benefits.
options.C: External benefits exceeded $200m.

questions.questionText: What is it called when a consumer’s marginal utility is greater than the price paid for the good?

options.A: a Giffen good
options.C: consumer surplus

questions.questionText: A consumer has $3 to spend each day on chocolate bars or toffee bars, which all cost $1 each. The table below shows the units of additional satisfaction she gets from consuming each bar. 1st chocolate bar 2nd chocolate bar 3rd chocolate bar
13 10 1st toffee bar 2nd toffee bar 3rd toffee bar
12 9 What should she buy to maximise her total utility?

options.A: 1 chocolate bar and 2 toffee bars
options.C: 3 chocolate bars

questions.questionText: The curve JK in the diagram is a consumer’s initial budget line. G good Y J O H K good X Which combination could cause the budget line to shift to GH? consumer’s price of good X money income

options.A: increase increase
options.C: increase decrease

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a consumer’s indifference curves (IC) for goods F and G together with the consumer’s budget lines. good F Z X IC Y 2 IC O good G What could explain the movement from X to Z on the diagram?

options.A: a fall in the price of G when G is an inferior good
options.B: a fall in the price of G when F is a Giffen good
options.C: a fall in the price of G when G is a normal good
options.D: a fall in the price of G when G is a Giffen good

questions.questionText: A firm has the choice between five levels of output. The table shows the total cost and total revenue of producing at each output level. The firm could sell whatever output it produces. output total cost total revenue (units) ($) ($) 1000 8000 10000 2000 12000 18000 3000 19000 24000 4000 23000 28000 5000 25000 25000 The firm decides to produce 4000 units. What is the firm’s aim?

options.A: to maximise profit
options.C: to maximise revenue

questions.questionText: In which type of market structure are commercial banks usually found?

options.A: perfect competition, because they all link their interest rates to that of the central bank
options.B: perfect competition, because they offer identical products and services
options.C: monopolistic competition, because a competitive market prevents them making excess profits
options.D: oligopoly, because they are affected by the actions of other banks

questions.questionText: What is a condition for operating a successful cartel?

options.A: a large number of firms in the industry
options.B: each firm has a differentiated product
options.C: low barriers of entry to the industry

questions.questionText: Which assumption is essential for a market to be contestable?

options.A: The market is supplied by a large number of firms.
options.B: Firms are free to enter and leave the market.
options.C: Firms cannot earn abnormal profits in the short run.

questions.questionText: What is generally associated with the principal-agent problem?

options.A: Directors prefer company growth to greater shareholder dividends.
options.B: Managers ignore workers’ concerns about safety in the workplace.
options.C: Shareholders determine the price of products.
options.D: Workers go on strike against managers’ reorganisation plans.

questions.questionText: The table shows the output of chairs at a factory when different numbers of workers are employed. number of workers 0 1 2 3 4 5 number of chairs produced 0 7 17 26 34 40 When will diminishing marginal returns to labour set in?

options.A: When the second worker is employed.
options.B: When the third worker is employed.
options.C: When the fourth worker is employed.
options.D: When the fifth worker is employed.

questions.questionText: A country has a negative income tax regime. The curve NT in the diagram shows the country’s initial tax schedule. + NT tax NT O income –

options.A: strengthen less equal
options.C: weaken less equal

questions.questionText: A government is worried about the increasing monopsony power of employers in the wage bargaining process. Which policy combination is most likely to improve the wages and employment prospects of workers? trade union immigration national powers controls minimum wage

options.A: strengthen relax cut
options.C: weaken relax cut

questions.questionText: What is not a source of market failure?

options.A: imperfect information
options.C: monopoly

questions.questionText: A government regards fresh fruit and vegetables as merit goods, and subsidises agriculture to boost their production. What could be a government failure arising from these subsidies?

options.A: cheaper fresh fruit and vegetables
options.C: lower spending on treating dietary illnesses
options.D: more jobs picking fruit and vegetables

questions.questionText: Which type of unemployment is associated with a deficiency in aggregate demand?

options.A: cyclical
options.C: structural

questions.questionText: In the diagram, OP is the equilibrium level of income and OQ the full employment level of income in a closed economy. expenditure V U C + I + G T C + I R C 45° O P Q income What is the deflationary gap?

options.A: PQ B RV C TV D UV

questions.questionText: What represents an injection into a country’s circular flow of income?

options.A: corporate taxes
options.C: the payment of dividends to foreign shareholders

questions.questionText: What will be the most likely consequence of an increase in the dependency ratio?

options.A: a decrease in GDP per head
options.C: an increase in the labour force

questions.questionText: Which statement is correct?

options.A: Economic development is necessary for economic growth.
options.B: Economic growth and economic development are directly proportional.
options.C: Economic growth enables economic development.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a production possibility curve PPC . The economy is initially at point X. If the economy achieves actual economic growth but not potential growth, what would the final position be? capital PPC goods PPC B C A X D O consumer goods
It has been estimated by the United Nations that the total external debt of developing countries has been increasing by about $425 billion each year. What is least likely to have contributed to this?

options.A: disincentives for foreign direct investment through political instability
options.B: increased government subsidies for the development of tourism industries
options.C: withdrawal of multinational companies due to delays in the award of government contracts
options.D: worsening of the terms of trade with partners in developed economies

questions.questionText: The following are four conditions sometimes attached to IMF loans to developing countries. Which condition would conflict with the ‘infant industry’ argument?

options.A: the need to allow free trade
options.C: the need to have a contractionary fiscal policy
options.D: the need to privatise government enterprises

questions.questionText: In which exchange rate regime would the central bank of a country be best able to pursue an independent monetary policy to control the rate of inflation?

options.A: a freely floating exchange rate system
options.B: a system where the country’s currency has a targeted value in relation to the US$
options.C: a system where the central bank buys and sells foreign currency at a fixed rate
options.D: where the country participates in a monetary union with other countries

questions.questionText: What is measured on the vertical axis of the Phillips curve?

options.A: the rate of change of real wages
options.B: the rate of change of take-home pay
options.C: the rate of inflation

questions.questionText: Workers in poor countries are often less productive than workers using the same technology in rich countries. What would be most likely to remedy this situation?

options.A: an increase in the saving ratio in poor countries
options.B: increased freedom of migration from poor countries to rich countries
options.C: increased investment in education in poor countries
